source_evidence.observation: The standing model uses one working precision, denotes its floating-point set by F, its relative rounding-error unit by eps, and its underflow unit by eta. IEEE 754 arithmetic is assumed, overflow is excluded, and underflow is allowed.

The notation fl(.) means that all operations inside the parentheses execute in working precision. For addition and subtraction the paper gives both relative-error bounds, states that these operations are exact in case of underflow, and describes a+b=x+y with x=fl(a+b) as an error-free transformation and a mathematical identity.
TwoSum computes x=fl(a+b), z=fl(x-a), and y=fl((a-(x-z))+(b-z)). Its outputs are working-precision floating-point numbers satisfying a+b=x+y and x=fl(a+b), including in the presence of underflow.
For every a,b in F and the outputs x,y of Algorithm 3.1, also in the presence of underflow, a+b=x+y, x=fl(a+b), |y|<=eps|x|, and |y|<=eps|a+b|. TwoSum requires six floating-point operations.

For floating-point inputs p_i, 1<=i<=n, the exact real sum is s=sum_{i=1}^n p_i. Cascaded TwoSum calls produce an ordinary sequential floating-point sum pi_n and residuals q_i with the exact identity s=pi_n+sum_{i=2}^n q_i.
The paper presents the transformation from the input n-vector p to [q_2,...,q_n,pi_n] as a two-part result: (i) sum_{i=1}^n p_i=sum_{i=2}^n q_i+pi_n=s, and (ii) pi_n=fl(sum_{i=1}^n p_i).

VecSum overwrites p in ascending iterations i=2:n using [p_i,p_{i-1}]=TwoSum(p_i,p_{i-1}). The paper explicitly says that this transformation does not change the sum and that the final p_n is the ordinary floating-point sum.

binders: For every pair a,b in the working-precision floating-point set F, x and y are the outputs produced by Algorithm 3.1 (TwoSum); they are generated outputs rather than independently chosen witnesses. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.2)]

For the vector result, an n-vector p=(p_1,...,p_n) of working-precision floating-point inputs is given, with indices 1<=i<=n, and s denotes the exact real sum sum_{i=1}^n p_i. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Section 4 opening and Algorithm 4.1]
The quantities q_2,...,q_n and pi_n are the outputs generated by the successive TwoSum calls; the transformed vector is [q_2,...,q_n,pi_n]. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7) and Algorithm 4.3]
hypotheses: The inherited standing model assumes one working precision and no overflow during the floating-point computation, while allowing underflow. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, Section 2, Notation]

TwoSum is specifically Algorithm 3.1: x=fl(a+b), z=fl(x-a), and y=fl((a-(x-z))+(b-z)), with all enclosed operations executed in working precision. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 1961, Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, definition of fl(.)]

VecSum is specifically the in-place ascending loop for i=2:n with [p_i,p_{i-1}]=TwoSum(p_i,p_{i-1}); both the argument order and output-slot order are part of the displayed algorithm. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]

No magnitude ordering, sorting, sign condition, noncancellation condition, or n*eps smallness condition is stated for equations (3.2) or (4.7). [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)]
conclusions: The local transformation is exact: a+b=x+y as an equality of real values. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.2)]
The leading TwoSum output is the computed working-precision sum: x=fl(a+b). [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.2)]
The residual satisfies both stated bounds, separately: |y|<=eps|x| and |y|<=eps|a+b|. Neither bound may be discarded. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.2)]

At every VecSum iteration, the instantiated TwoSum identity preserves the exact sum of the two overwritten slots; its second output is the exact residual associated with the first output. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]
After all iterations, the exact input sum is decomposed as sum_{i=1}^n p_i=sum_{i=2}^n q_i+pi_n=s. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]

The other part of equation (4.7) states pi_n=fl(sum_{i=1}^n p_i), where the algorithmic context identifies pi_n as the ordinary sequential working-precision sum in input order. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Algorithm 4.1 and eq. (4.1); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(ii)]

Equivalently for the in-place VecSum output, p_1 through p_{n-1} contain q_2 through q_n, p_n contains pi_n, and the exact sum of all output entries equals the exact sum of all input entries. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7) and Algorithm 4.3]
TwoSum has the stated operation count of six floating-point operations. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, text following eq. (3.2)]
definitions_and_conventions: F is the set of working-precision floating-point numbers, eps is the relative rounding-error unit, and eta is the underflow unit. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, Section 2, Notation]

fl(.) denotes a floating-point computation in which every operation inside the parentheses is performed in the one working precision; parentheses disambiguate execution order when necessary. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, opening of Section 2 continuation]

Unadorned equalities and sums such as a+b=x+y and s=sum p_i are mathematical identities over real values, not additional rounded operations. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, discussion of eq. (2.3); PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, eq. (4.2)]
An error-free transformation preserves all information by representing the exact input sum as the exact real sum of floating-point outputs. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, discussion following eq. (2.3)]

Algorithm 4.3 reuses the symbol p for both input storage and overwritten output storage; equation (4.7) describes the input values on its left and the generated residual/accumulator values on its right. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7) and Algorithm 4.3]
implicit_context: The index notation and the phrase n-vector imply that n is a positive integer, although no separate quantified declaration n in N is printed beside Algorithm 4.3. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Section 4 opening; PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)]

During the ascending in-place loop, the current p_i is the next untouched input and the current p_{i-1} is the accumulated leading sum; after the call, the leading sum is stored in p_i and its residual in p_{i-1}. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]

The compact notation fl(sum p_i) in equation (4.7)(ii) inherits the order fixed by the ascending cascade, rather than permitting an arbitrary permutation or reduction tree. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Algorithm 4.1 and eq. (4.1); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]

The TwoProduct portions of Theorem 3.4 are separate multiplication results and are not used by VecSum, whose loop calls only TwoSum. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4; PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Equation (3.2) is the contract of the exact Algorithm 3.1 TwoSum variant. Algorithm 4.1 cascades that operation and derives the exact decomposition in equation (4.2). Equation (4.7) restates the resulting vector transformation, and Algorithm 4.3 is explicitly the in-place rewrite of Algorithm 4.1's first part. Thus VecSum's global sum preservation is obtained by successive applications of the local TwoSum identity, not by an unrelated summation specification. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 1961, Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2); PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Algorithm 4.1 and eq. (4.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7) and Algorithm 4.3]
numerical_model: The explicit standing model is IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic with one working precision, no overflow, and possible underflow. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, Section 2, Notation]

For addition and subtraction, the paper uses |a op b-fl(a op b)|<=eps|a op b| and <=eps|fl(a op b)|, and states that addition and subtraction are exact in case of underflow. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, eq. (2.1) and surrounding text]

The TwoSum and VecSum computations use addition and subtraction only; consequently equation (3.2) remains exact in the presence of underflow and contains no additive eta term. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 1961, Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2)]

The paper notes that IEEE 754 itself is unnecessary if an operation satisfying the stated error-free TwoSum transformation is available. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, final paragraph of Section 2 opening]
error_notions: The primary local notion is error-free transformation: y is the exact real correction a+b-x to the rounded leading result x. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2)]
The two local inequalities bound the absolute residual relative respectively to the computed leading value and the exact sum. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2)]
The vector claim is exact sum preservation and exact residual decomposition, not merely a forward-, backward-, componentwise-, or normwise-error inequality. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]

Equation (4.7)(ii) separately identifies the final leading component as the computed ordinary floating-point sum; it is not the assertion that this component alone equals the exact sum. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(ii)]
norms: The selected local result uses only scalar absolute value in |y|, |x|, and |a+b|. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2)]
The selected vector invariant uses an exact scalar sum and specifies no vector norm. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]
constants_and_indexing: Both residual bounds in equation (3.2) have coefficient exactly one times eps. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2)]
VecSum iterates with i=2,3,...,n, not from i=1, and writes the residual from iteration i into slot i-1. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]
The transformed vector is indexed [q_2,...,q_n,pi_n], so the exact decomposition sums residuals from 2 through n and then adds pi_n. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]
The first TwoSum output is written to p_i and the second to p_{i-1}; reversing those outputs would not be the displayed algorithm. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]
The stated cost of a TwoSum call is six floating-point operations. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, text following eq. (3.2)]
higher_order_terms: Equation (3.2) contains exact identities and explicit first-order eps bounds with no omitted O(eps^2) or other higher-order term. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2)]
Equation (4.7)(i) is an exact equality with no eps-dependent remainder, eta term, asymptotic qualification, or big-O term. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]
No accumulated global residual bound is part of the selected VecSum invariant; only the exact decomposition and ordinary-sum identification are asserted there. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)]
exceptional_values: Overflow is excluded by the paper's standing assumptions. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, Section 2, Notation]

Underflow, including gradual underflow relevant to the working format, is allowed, and the TwoSum theorem explicitly remains valid in its presence. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 1961, discussion after eq. (3.1); PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4]

The selected passages do not specify behavior for NaNs, infinities, signaling exceptions, or the sign of zero; their equations interpret floating-point quantities as real values. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, discussion after eq. (2.2); PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, definition s=sum p_i in R]

undebatable_constraints: The local primitive must be the displayed three-line Algorithm 3.1 TwoSum, not FastTwoSum, TwoSumADD3, or an unspecified approximate addition. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 1961, Algorithm 3.1]

For every permitted input pair, all four clauses of equation (3.2) must be retained: exact decomposition, rounded leading output, and both residual bounds. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.2)]
The TwoSum result requires no input magnitude ordering such as |a|>=|b|. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.2)]
The VecSum loop order is ascending i=2:n and its call is [p_i,p_{i-1}]=TwoSum(p_i,p_{i-1}). [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, Algorithm 4.3]
The global output is an n-term representation [q_2,...,q_n,pi_n] whose exact real sum equals the exact real sum of the input vector. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]

Equation (4.7)(ii) must be retained alongside part (i): pi_n is the ordinary sequential working-precision sum produced by the cascade. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Algorithm 4.1 and eq. (4.1); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(ii)]
Exact sums on the two sides of equation (4.7)(i) are real-arithmetic sums, not separately rounded reductions. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, eq. (4.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]
The result explicitly covers underflow but inherits the standing exclusion of overflow. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, Section 2; PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4]
No hypothesis n*eps<1 and no global normwise error estimate belongs to the exact claims in equations (3.2) and (4.7). [PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)]
The exact vector identity has no omitted error, higher-order term, or underflow correction. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7)(i)]

ambiguities.issue: The exact admissible lower bound on n is implicit rather than separately quantified.
ambiguities.evidence: Section 4 introduces p_i for 1<=i<=n, while VecSum loops over i=2:n and equation (4.7) sums q_i from 2 to n; the paper does not explicitly discuss the n=1 boundary case at this passage. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Section 4 opening; PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7) and Algorithm 4.3]
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract must either admit n=1 using the standard empty-loop and empty-sum conventions or explicitly restrict to n>=2; it should not choose silently.

ambiguities.issue: The theorem does not restate an exact rounding mode or radix beside equation (3.2).
ambiguities.evidence: The standing section says IEEE 754 arithmetic and supplies the eps error model, while Theorem 3.4 simply invokes that context and states the TwoSum guarantee, including underflow. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, Section 2; PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, eq. (2.1); PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, Theorem 3.4]
ambiguities.impact: A low-level formalization should not claim that the displayed implementation is valid under every possible radix and rounding mode without an additional justification; alternatively it may assume the equation (3.2) TwoSum contract directly.

ambiguities.issue: The in-place notation does not use distinct symbols for the input and output vectors.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (4.7) describes an input vector p transformed into [q_2,...,q_n,pi_n], but Algorithm 4.3 is written as function p=VecSum(p) and overwrites p at each iteration. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7) and Algorithm 4.3]
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement should snapshot or separately name the original vector so that sum preservation does not accidentally compare the output vector with itself.

ambiguities.issue: IEEE exceptional values and signed-zero semantics are not specified.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper names F as the set of working-precision floating-point numbers but expresses the relevant exact sums as elements or identities in R and discusses only overflow and underflow among exceptional cases. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 1959, Section 2; PDF p. 6, printed p. 1960, discussion after eq. (2.2); PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, definition of s]
ambiguities.impact: A faithful real-valued formalization should restrict to finite numeric values or explicitly explain how NaNs, infinities, and signed zeros are abstracted.

contract_plain_english: Given two working-precision floating-point numbers, the paper's exact Three-line TwoSum algorithm returns a rounded leading sum and a floating-point residual whose exact real sum equals the exact input sum; the residual obeys both coefficient-one eps bounds, and the result remains valid with underflow but under the standing no-overflow assumption. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 1961, Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 8, printed p. 1962, eq. (3.2)] VecSum applies that precise operation in place for i=2 through n, storing each residual one slot to the left and carrying the rounded partial sum to the right. Its final vector [q_2,...,q_n,pi_n] has exactly the same real sum as the original vector, while pi_n is separately identified as the ordinary sequential working-precision sum. These are exact identities with no global error remainder, big-O term, eta correction, magnitude-order requirement, or n*eps smallness premise. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 1963, Algorithm 4.1 and eqs. (4.1)-(4.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 1965, eq. (4.7) and Algorithm 4.3]
